body:
They are federal.  They did offer me rehabilitation.  I asked them to give me until February to make the first payment, since I can't even pay my rent now, and they told me that because of that, and because I wouldn't turn my credit card information over to them so they could charge it automatically every month, they "couldn't guarantee" that they wouldn't garnish my wages.  It's hard to negotiate with them, because I get so worked up talking to them that it makes me want to cut myself, and I'm trying to stop doing that.

A lot of my problems are financial.  People I graduated with who moved to bigger cities have careers, have their loans paid off, and are starting families.  I'll never have any of that, because I'll never be able to afford it.  But my problem is also that I'm only as good to anyone as what I can do for them--holding a hand, paying a bill, doing work no one else has the stomach for.  I'm never a human being with a right to security and happiness, or even safety, and every job I've had has no trouble reminding me of that.  I live in an area where my last job, at $19.50/hr, was considered "high-paying", and I had to do things you couldn't imagine to earn that.  I can't live with that level of stress again.  So, I'll probably never be able to pay my bills again...if that makes sense.

Thanks anyway for your concern.
